outcomes.title: Government is Accountable to Deliver
outcomes.desc: Governments uphold their human rights obligations by assessing the situation, and publicly documenting their findings and commitments to acheive measurable results. This includes coordinated action and transparent accountability across departments.

outcomes.title: Community Wealth and Inclusive Local Economies
outcomes.desc: Residents and community organizations build and retain economic assets, access decent jobs and affordable commercial opportunities, and share equitably in the benefits of investment.

outcomes.title: Right to Remain and Return
outcomes.desc: Existing residents and businesses are protected from displacement and have meaningful, affordable opportunities to remain or return as their neighbourhood changes.

outcomes.title: Community Decision-Making and Reparative Justice
outcomes.desc: Residents and community organizations exercise meaningful authority over planning and implementation; Indigenous rights and governance are respected, and public institutions acknowledge and remedy harms caused by past decisions.

outcomes.title: Belonging and Cultural Continuity
outcomes.desc: Residents experience belonging, see their histories and contributions recognized, and sustain the cultural practices, institutions and community relationships that connect them to place.

outcomes.title: Adequate Standard of Living and Wellbeing
outcomes.desc: Residents have access to affordable and appropriate housing, essential services, safe mobility and healthy, climate-resilient living conditions, including support for multigenerational households, older adults and people experiencing homelessness.

aggregation: each completed response contributes once; provisional averages available from first completion
explicitChoice: Six suggested highest-priority survey topics from six Planning Area rankings and six community outcome rankings; residents can move suggestions to middle or add other topics to their highest six, then select two lowest-priority topics from the remaining fourteen, leaving twelve middle priorities.
outcomeAssignmentPolicy: Twenty public survey topics map without overlap to thirty-three detailed assessment criteria. Each detailed criterion retains exactly one primary community outcome; survey topics may span multiple outcomes. Outcome shares within a survey topic are proportional to its constituent criteria. Rights obligations remain cross-cutting, not optional. The four outcome reassigments adopted November 10, 2026: CB-03 and NE-01 -> belong, NE-05 -> wellbeing, CP-03 -> power.
humanRightsLens: All six outcomes must respect applicable housing and human rights obligations, confront anti-Black and anti-Indigenous racism and other systemic discrimination, address accessibility, and respect distinct Indigenous rights, treaties and governance. Detailed rights assessment criteria remain RJ-02 and RJ-03; priorities do not diminish obligations.
suggestionFormula: Score = 100 * (0.6 * (Planning Area rank points - 4) / 5 + 0.4 * sum(outcome criterion share * (outcome rank points - 1) / 5)). Planning Area ranks 1-6 have points 9-4; outcome ranks 1-6 have points 6-1. This orders six provisional highest choices; final weight pools are 60% highest six, 37% middle twelve and 3% lowest two. Underlying 33 documentary criteria share each survey topic's weight equally; no combined topic receives extra weight solely because it contains more criteria.

scoringPolicy.criterionRule: Each survey topic receives one priority weight. For each documentary comparator, the topic score is the arithmetic mean of its linked underlying criterion ratings; the framework total is the weighted sum across the 20 topics.
scoringPolicy.outcomeRule: Allocate each survey topic's weighted contribution across outcomes according to constituent criterion counts, preserving exact total contribution.
scoringPolicy.crossVersion: New methodology ID isolates responses and community averages from 33-topic survey versions.
